summary: Flyway migrations never ran; app failed fast with a schema-validation error instead
repro: mvn verify with Postgres+Redis wired, flyway-core on classpath
expected: Flyway migrates the schema on startup before Hibernate validates it
actual: Hibernate validate failed: missing table [close_event_entity] etc - Flyway silently never executed
root_cause: Spring Boot 4 split its monolithic autoconfigure jar per feature; flyway-core alone does not carry org.springframework.boot.flyway.autoconfigure.FlywayAutoConfiguration - that now lives in a separate spring-boot-flyway artifact which was missing

summary: onClose threw UnexpectedRollbackException under real Postgres, breaking every ledger update
repro: Call onClose twice in sequence within one @Transactional method, or read the ledger back via findById
root_cause: @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) override on DayLedgerRepository.findById issued SELECT...FOR UPDATE in a context Hibernate/Postgres rejected under this combination, poisoning the surrounding transaction
fix: Removed the pessimistic-lock override; cross-replica serialisation is handled by the Redis PortfolioLock instead, which already covers single-underlying concurrency since one underlying's correlation group always includes itself
retest: FIXED - both tests pass against real Postgres

severity: P3 (test hygiene - not a production defect)
summary: A direct PortfolioLock test left the real 'india_equity_index' lock held for its TTL, causing every other test's approve() call in the suite to be falsely rejected with 'another decision in flight'
repro: Run the full IT suite; order-dependent failure depending on which test executes within the TTL window
expected: Each test is independent of every other test's side effects
actual: 5 of 11 tests failed with 'Another decision is already in flight...' though the underlying logic was correct
root_cause: The lock test used the SAME correlation-group name real approve() calls use, and never released the final lock it acquired
fix: Isolated the test to its own group name ('test_only_group'), and wrapped every acquire in try/finally so it always releases

summary: /api/risk/close used the SERVER's wall-clock time instead of the broker event's own timestamp, so a close processed even slightly after midnight (or any replayed/delayed event) silently posted to the WRONG trading day's ledger - meaning the daily-loss-limit and consecutive-loss protections could silently fail to trigger on the day they actually should
repro: Close a position with pnl that should trip the daily loss limit, then try to open a new position on the SAME calendar day the loss happened on
expected: The day's ledger reflects the loss; the next decision on that day is blocked
actual: Decision on the correct day showed an EMPTY ledger - the close had been recorded under the container's current wall-clock date
root_cause: not the date I told the decision endpoint about
files_changed: RiskController.close() called LocalDateTime.now() instead of accepting the event's own timestamp as a parameter, unlike /api/risk/decision which already took 'now' explicitly
regression_test: Added a required 'occurredAt' request parameter; onClose now always books against the event's own time
retest: Live-verified via curl against the running dev compose stack (see test-execution-report.md); no automated IT test added for this exact controller behaviour - flagged as a residual test gap
column13: FIXED and manually verified live; automated regression test still owed

summary: FIFO engine (build_episodes) had no duplicate-fill protection: the same broker trade_id fed in twice (re-run import, overlapping export, replayed event) silently doubled the realised P&L for that fill
repro: Feed the same Trade object (same trade_id) into build_episodes twice
expected: The duplicate is ignored; P&L is unaffected
actual: P&L for the affected episode doubled relative to the single-copy case
root_cause: No idempotency/dedup step existed anywhere in the pipeline
fix: Added dedupe_by_trade_id() called at the start of build_episodes; drops exact trade_id repeats (blank ids are never treated as duplicates of each other)

summary: Each Compose profile's Spring config pointed at a differently-named Postgres database (pie_trader / pie_trader_test / pie_trader_paper) but the Postgres container only ever creates ONE database at first init, named by POSTGRES_DB - every non-dev profile crash-looped on 'database does not exist'
actual: FATAL: database 'pie_trader_paper' does not exist - crash loop
root_cause: POSTGRES_DB env was never overridden per-profile to match that profile's application-<profile>.yml datasource URL
fix: Added a matching POSTGRES_DB override to the postgres service in each profile file
regression_test: Live-verified: all 4 profiles built fresh and reached /actuator/health = UP (see test-execution-report.md)

summary: test/integration profiles could not reach Redis: the app defaulted to the HOST-remapped Redis port (6380) instead of the container-internal port (6379) that the Docker network actually uses between containers
root_cause: application-test.yml's PIE_REDIS_PORT default (6380) was meant for a bare local run against a remapped host port, not for traffic inside the compose network, which always reaches redis on its own internal 6379
fix: Overrode PIE_REDIS_PORT=6379 for risk-engine in both profile files
regression_test: Live-verified: both profiles reached /actuator/health = UP and answered a real /api/risk/decision call
